title: About
text:
This page exists to round out the minimal website. Together with the Home page, it demonstrates three things:

Multi-page project rendering. Running quarto render on the project directory walks every .qmd, builds a project-wide index of document profiles, and renders each page with that index in scope.
Manual sidebar configuration. A website.sidebar.contents: list whose entries are bare .qmd paths produces a working sidebar with one entry per page. The visible label comes from the target page’s title:.
Cross-document link rewriting. When you write [About](about.qmd) in a paragraph, the rendered HTML contains <a href="about.html">. The same is true of the link back to [Home](index.qmd) above. You don’t need to write the .html extension yourself — and you shouldn’t, because the source path is what’s stable across format choices.

title: Home
text:
This is the minimal Quarto 2 website example. It contains two pages and one sidebar.
The sidebar is configured manually in _quarto.yml:
website:
  sidebar:
    contents:
      - index.qmd
      - about.qmd
Both entries are bare paths. Their visible text comes from each page’s title: frontmatter — no explicit text: is needed. The sidebar links resolve to the rendered HTML (about.html), not the source path (about.qmd).
Visit the About page to read about the features this example demonstrates.
